observations: The routine writes nothing back to the object: no field is cleared and no size is reset.
The +0x98 cell delete is guarded, not plain: a nonzero first qword ends the process via std::terminate instead of freeing anything, and no later phase runs.
The +0x40 condition-variable destroy is unconditional: it runs even when every pointer field is null, because the variable is inline, not a pointer.
The +0x18 array free is a tail jump to the delete[] stub, while the +0x38 and +0x28 frees are direct calls; the distinction is not observable in the event order.

The wrapper's trailing endbr64 plus jump fragment at 0x60d54f7 jumps to 0x60d545c, a dispose-then-terminate fragment of the preceding function; it is not on the wrapper's normal or abort return paths.

The release helper 0x5d350c0 is pinned by call shape only here; its internal release contract (64-bit count at +0x08, destroy at zero) is established in the RE-001 derived-destructor packet for the same helper address.
The wrapper's diagnostic helper 0x61d1f30 is pinned by call shape only; only its position in the abort path is claimed.

Both consumers sit in teardown sequences of a larger rbx holder: each first destroys two +0x920/+0x888-style subobjects through the 0x5d5b300/0x5d5b4c0 pair, then calls this routine, then releases the holder +0x758 pointer through the shared helper and calls 0x60d5170 on +0x700; caller bodies beyond those sites are not pinned.
